name: Night of Armageddon

date.source: The fed's own served broadcast dates itself "Night of Armageddon — March 20th, 1999", live from the Cox Arena, San Diego, California.

matches.note: One-pinfall, thirty-minute time limit. Banshee wins with a top-rope "Banshee Buster," driving the Immature Child's back across his knee.

Called by Jaigo himself at the bell. The M.o.A (led by Flesh, who delivers his own brick and blow to Jaigo — see this show's own angle appearance) buries Jaigo under a dropped pile of bricks before Riley pins him; Riley never takes a scripted offensive move of his own beyond the cover.

No time limit; billed the BEW Television Title (see bew-television — the fed's own card page conflictingly labels this the Hardcore Title Match, receipted at bew-hardcore). Both men fall through live land mines; Extreme Warrior nails Prophet's hands and feet to a wooden cross mid-match before pulling him down and finishing him with a hammer blow.

One-pinfall, sixty-minute time limit; the BEW United States Title. The fed's own commentary calls it Pope's first match in the BEW. Pope wins with the Limo Wreck (a double-underhook facebuster) after a guardrail brawl on the outside.

Minister of Violence is announced as "an M.o.A turncoat." Matt Attic distracts him from ringside with a threatening promo ("Leon... I have a message for you"), letting Mass Carnage finish him with a Sweet Dreams pinwheel kick.

The BEW World Title (see bew-world); the fed's own broadcast calls it "the header to the main event." Devastator never appears in person, cutting his own promo by remote screen from the crowd before Jamie Williams pins him with a Northern Lights Elbow; the M.o.A then floods the ring and beats Devastator down further after the bell.

The show's own main event, billed with no title at stake by either the broadcast's own introduction or the fed's own card page (SOURCES DISAGREE with this wing's own tier-1 pass, which had read it as a BEW World Title match; corrected — see bew-world). Merrix wins with two Fallout finishers (a reverse Ligerbomb). Post-match: the M.o.A floods the ring and beats Merrix down; a cloaked figure revealed as Saleah Ridgers directs the assault before Merrix unmasks her; Styx then returns to the promotion for the first time this broadcast, ordering "Break him"; a five-man save (Vigilance, Chris Anderson, Brian Anderson, Richard Hope, and a freed Greg Eskridge) clears the ring before the broadcast ends.

notes: The fed's own flagship 1999 PPV, billed "a joint venture" between BEW and the Masters of Armageddon (M.o.A) stable, called by BEW President Michael Merrix and Big Hughy ("the Voice of the M.o.A"). Michael Merrix and main-eventer Kevin Merrix are billed on-air as brothers. A satellite interview segment mid-show features Jose Gonzalez, billed leader of the M.o.A's own Mexican contingent, announcing a unified "My Title" across Mexico's wrestling federations — not itself a BEW title and not structured as one. Greg Eskridge, the show's own ring announcer, is revealed mid-broadcast to have turned on BEW President Merrix and his brother Kevin, engineering the M.o.A's own post-match beatdown of Kevin Merrix before delivering the finishing blow himself; he is freed only by the closing save. THE TITLE-MATCH CORRECTION (2026-09-01): a full cold re-read of both the broadcast and the fed's own card page found the wing's own tier-1 pass had misattributed the night's BEW World Title match to the Flesh/Merrix main event — the card's own section header ("BEW World Title Match") in fact precedes the Jamie Williams/Devastator bout, one match earlier, exactly as the broadcast's own "header to the main event" line independently confirms; the Flesh/Merrix bout itself carries no title stakes in either document. The reign ledger (see bew-world) and Kevin Merrix's/Jamie Williams's own tenures are corrected accordingly. The fed's own card page also labels the Extreme Warrior/Jonathan Prophet crucifixion match "BEW Hardcore Title Match," contradicted by the broadcast's own repeated and internally consistent dialogue naming it a Television Title defense (Flesh is separately and consistently billed the show's own current Hardcore champion, entering a later match, which the card's own label would put in direct conflict) — both documents are receipted at bew-television/bew-hardcore, neither silently resolved.
